correctness.rationale: The exact norm-subgradient condition \(u\perp_B v\) iff the signed support sum lies within the missing-coordinate magnitude sum is proved. Coordinate axes restrict all other vertices to a two-dimensional coordinate plane, giving at most three lines; a full-support vector permits at most three two-support and one more full-support line, giving at most five; with neither type, the six signed two-support types give an absolute bound of six. Two orthogonality directions for each support pair force balanced lines, proving uniqueness. Every pair of the six stated lines satisfies the criterion. The checker independently evaluates 15,376 derivative inequalities, 13 ternary sign types and the single size-six ternary clique but is not used as an infinite certificate.

value.rationale: The first dimension past the normed-plane case is a natural complete test of nonsmooth mutual orthogonality. Six strictly exceeds the vector-space dimension three and is the exact maximum over an uncountable projective graph, not a selected ternary graph. Uniqueness forces all maximizers to be the three pairs of balanced coordinate-plane diagonals, supplying a rigid base case for higher-dimensional taxicab clique bounds and distinguishing it from both generic dimension bounds and asymptotic existence proofs.
